queries.method: One buildIndex into a scratch cache per tree, then a fresh Node process per measurement: loadIndex (timed), the first index.edges.length access (timed; realizes the lazy edges.json read on the optimized tree, already realized on the baseline tree), the first ask(index, "resolve import path from stub file", { limit: 5 }) (timed), then the first and second scopedAsk(index, "resolve import path") in the same process (timed). Each of the three trials per tree is a separate fresh-process run against a freshly rebuilt scratch cache; medians are reported.

method: Same host, pinned source and dependencies; disposable scratch caches; one initial build; seven warm no-change refreshes and seven one-file edited refreshes with untimed restoration/equality verification; nearest-rank p95; filesystem caches not flushed. Baseline built from the commit before this task set (af40f15); optimized built from the tip of this branch (2b06e03). Both runs used the same disposable checkout and the same manifest snapshot fingerprint, invoked through the harness's own documented --worker mode directly (same arguments the non-worker CLI wrapper would pass) because the baseline tree's full seven-sample run exceeds the wrapper's 60-second child-process timeout (scripts/bench/cli.ts). No harness file was modified. Section sizes and cold-query timings were measured separately from the harness with small scripts against each tree's dist/index.js, since the harness reports only serializedArtifactBytes/storedArtifactBytes for the structural core and no per-file query timings; those scripts are not part of the committed record.
limitations: editedRefreshMs regressed on this workload relative to the pre-task-set baseline (median -4.10%, p95 -3.21%) while noChangeRefreshMs improved marginally (median +0.64%, p95 +0.92%); format 9's lazy edges, string tables and copy-on-publish target artifact size, memory and cold-query latency, not edited-refresh wall time, and the extra index.sha and edges.json writes on a dirty refresh add file-system overhead the format-8 single-file core did not have.

Cold ask() latency is roughly unchanged between trees (before median 743.20ms, after median 753.14ms); the per-file document cache that helps warm asks does not help a fully cold first query, and format 9's smaller core reduces parse cost but not the extraction/indexing cost that dominates a cold ask.

The benchmark harness (scripts/bench/runner.ts) has no scopedAsk case kind, so scopedAsk timings and hit counts come only from the separate cold-query script, not from the recorded harness cases; the round-robin scope merge from the prior commit was reverted pending a scoped-ask acceptance gate (see benchmarks/results/scope-ranking-2026-09-15.json), so these scopedAsk numbers reflect round-robin merge behavior, not the reverted comparable-score candidate.
The benchmark is one repository and one machine with warm filesystem caches, not a universal latency claim.

incrementalEqualsFull, lazyEdgesVerified and copyOnPublishVerified are established by the repository's own test suite (test/incremental.test.ts's determinism and randomized incremental-equals-full property test; test/copy-on-publish.test.ts's shared-file-descriptor publish test; test/artifact-format9.test.ts's lazy edges.json load test), not re-verified independently by this record; probeFirstVerified is established by test/probe-first.test.ts.

workerPeakRssBytes and firstBuildMs are reported by the harness but not the primary subject of this record; baseline (af40f15) firstBuildMs 3920.541583 and workerPeakRssBytes 1398030336, optimized (2b06e03) firstBuildMs 4077.489708 and workerPeakRssBytes 1226293248.
